title: Ensure that authentication is enabled for Cassandra databases
description: Authentication is pluggable in Cassandra and is configured using the authenticator setting in cassandra.yaml. Cassandra ships with two options included in the default distribution, AllowAllAuthenticator and PasswordAuthenticator. The default, AllowAllAuthenticator, performs no authentication checks and therefore requires no credentials. It is used to disable authentication completely. Checks /etc/cassandra/cassandra.yaml (package install; SKIP when it does not exist).
reference: CIS Apache Cassandra 5.0 Benchmark v1.1.0 - 2.1 Ensure that authentication is enabled for Cassandra databases

remediation.command: Set 'authenticator: PasswordAuthenticator' in cassandra.yaml, raise system_auth replication (NetworkTopologyStrategy, RF 3 per DC), rolling-restart the nodes and create a new superuser.

title: Ensure that authorization is enabled for Cassandra databases
description: Authorization is pluggable in Cassandra and is configured using the authorizer setting in cassandra.yaml. Cassandra ships with two options included in the default distribution, AllowAllAuthenticator and CassandraAuthorizer. The default, AllowAllAuthenticator performs no checking which grants all permissions to all roles. Checks /etc/cassandra/cassandra.yaml (package install; SKIP when it does not exist).
reference: CIS Apache Cassandra 5.0 Benchmark v1.1.0 - 2.2 Ensure that authorization is enabled for Cassandra databases

remediation.command: Set 'authorizer: CassandraAuthorizer' in cassandra.yaml, rolling-restart the nodes, then grant least-privilege permissions to roles.

title: Ensure that the default password is changed for the cassandra role
description: The cassandra role has a default password which must be changed. Attempts a cqlsh login as cassandra/cassandra against CQLSH_HOST/CQLSH_PORT (default 127.0.0.1:9042); passes only when the server rejects the credentials (a login that succeeds, including with authentication disabled, fails; an unreachable node fails).
reference: CIS Apache Cassandra 5.0 Benchmark v1.1.0 - 3.2 Ensure that the default password is changed for the cassandra role

audit.command: command -v cqlsh >/dev/null 2>&1 || exit 1; out=$(cqlsh -u cassandra -p cassandra -e 'SELECT release_version FROM system.local;' 2>&1); rc=$?; if [ $rc -eq 0 ]; then echo default_password_accepted; elif printf '%s' "$out" | grep -qiE 'AuthenticationFailed|Bad credentials|incorrect'; then echo compliant; else exit 1; fi

remediation.command: Log in as a superuser and run ALTER ROLE cassandra WITH PASSWORD = '<new strong password>'; (or disable the role after creating a replacement superuser, see 3.1).

title: Ensure latest version of Cassandra is installed
description: The Cassandra installation version, along with the patches, should be the most recent that is compatible with organization's operational needs. When obtaining and installing software packages (typically via apt-get or you can compile the source code), it's imperative that packages (or the source code, tarball) are sourced only from valid and authorized repositories. Assessed manually here: the benchmark check is environment-specific and cannot be evaluated reliably by a single command.
reference: CIS Apache Cassandra 5.0 Benchmark v1.1.0 - 1.4 Ensure latest version of Cassandra is installed

audit.command: Run cassandra -v (or nodetool version) on every node and compare with the Apache Cassandra download page. The release must be a supported series and the latest patch of it; an old or unsupported version is a finding.

remediation.command: Upgrade to the latest version of the Cassandra software: For each node in the cluster: 1. Using the nodetool drain command to push all memtables data to SSTables. 2. Stop Cassandra services. 3. Backup the data set and all of your Cassandra configuration files. 4. Download/Update Java if needed. 5. Download/Update Python if needed. 6. Download the binaries for the latest Cassandra revision from the Cassandra Download Page. 7.

title: Ensure the Cassandra service is run as a non-root user
description: Though Cassandra database may be run as root, it should run as another non-root user. FAILs when no CassandraDaemon process is running.
reference: CIS Apache Cassandra 5.0 Benchmark v1.1.0 - 1.5 Ensure the Cassandra service is run as a non-root user

audit.command: out=$(ps -eo user=,args= | grep '[C]assandraDaemon') || exit 1; printf '%s\n' "$out" | awk '$1 == "root" {n++} END {print n+0}'

remediation.command: Create a dedicated cassandra system user, chown the data, commitlog, saved_caches and log directories to it and start the service with User=cassandra.

title: Ensure the cassandra and superuser roles are separate
description: The default installation of Cassandra includes a superuser role named cassandra. This necessitates the creation of a separate role to be the superuser role. Runs cqlsh against CQLSH_HOST/CQLSH_PORT (default 127.0.0.1:9042) with credentials from ~/.cassandra/cqlshrc ([authentication] username/password) of a superuser. Passes when the default cassandra role is not a superuser; also review the remaining superuser roles (3.8).
reference: CIS Apache Cassandra 5.0 Benchmark v1.1.0 - 3.1 Ensure the cassandra and superuser roles are separate

audit.command: out=$(cqlsh -e 'SELECT role FROM system_auth.roles WHERE is_superuser = True ALLOW FILTERING;' 2>/dev/null) || exit 1; printf '%s\n' "$out" | grep -cE '^[[:space:]]*cassandra[[:space:]]*$' || true

remediation.command: CREATE ROLE <admin> WITH PASSWORD = '<strong>' AND LOGIN = true AND SUPERUSER = true; GRANT ALL PERMISSIONS ON ALL KEYSPACES TO <admin>; log in as it and run ALTER ROLE cassandra WITH SUPERUSER = false AND LOGIN = false;

title: Ensure that Cassandra is run using a non-privileged, dedicated service account
description: As with any service installed on a host, it can be provided with its own user context. Providing a dedicated user to the service provides the ability to precisely constrain the service within the larger host context. Passes when every CassandraDaemon process runs as the cassandra account (the benchmark assumes that user name); also confirm with sudo -l -U cassandra that it has no administrative rights.
reference: CIS Apache Cassandra 5.0 Benchmark v1.1.0 - 3.4 Ensure that Cassandra is run using a non-privileged, dedicated service account

audit.command: out=$(ps -eo user=,args= | grep '[C]assandraDaemon') || exit 1; printf '%s\n' "$out" | awk '$1 != "cassandra" {n++} END {print n+0}'

remediation.command: Run Cassandra under a dedicated, non-administrative cassandra account (User=cassandra in the service unit) and remove any sudo rights for it.

title: Review Superuser/Admin Roles
description: The IS_SUPERUSER privilege found in the system_auth.roles table governs who can control the entire Cassandra database and all of its data contained within.
reference: CIS Apache Cassandra 5.0 Benchmark v1.1.0 - 3.8 Review Superuser/Admin Roles

audit.command: Execute the following SQL statement to audit this setting: select role, is_superuser from system_auth.roles; Looking for is_superuser = True

remediation.command: Perform the following steps to remediate this setting: Looking at those users from the query that have is_superuser = True, decide if that user truly needs that role, if not, for each user, issue the following SQL statement (replace <role> with the role name from the query): alter role <role> with superuser=false;

title: Ensure that auditing is enabled
description: Audit logging in Cassandra logs every incoming CQL command request, Authentication (successful as well as unsuccessful login) to C* node. Currently, there are two implementations provided, the custom logger can be implemented and injected with the class name as a parameter in cassandra.yaml. The benchmark rates this recommendation Manual; the automated check covers its objective pass criterion. Checks /etc/cassandra/cassandra.yaml (package install; SKIP when it does not exist).
reference: CIS Apache Cassandra 5.0 Benchmark v1.1.0 - 4.2 Ensure that auditing is enabled

remediation.command: Set audit_logging_options.enabled: true (logger BinAuditLogger or FileAuditLogger, with included_categories) in cassandra.yaml and restart, or run nodetool enableauditlog on each node.

title: Inter-node Encryption
description: Cassandra offers the option to encrypt data in transit between nodes on the cluster. By default, inter-node encryption is turned off. Checks /etc/cassandra/cassandra.yaml (package install; SKIP when it does not exist). Acceptable values are all, dc or rack.
reference: CIS Apache Cassandra 5.0 Benchmark v1.1.0 - 5.1 Inter-node Encryption

remediation.command: Build keystores/truststores, set server_encryption_options.internode_encryption: all in cassandra.yaml and rolling-restart all nodes.

title: Client Encryption
description: Cassandra offers the option to encrypt data in transit between the client and nodes on the cluster. By default client encryption is turned off. Checks /etc/cassandra/cassandra.yaml (package install; SKIP when it does not exist). Passes when client_encryption_options.enabled is true; set optional: false to refuse unencrypted clients.
reference: CIS Apache Cassandra 5.0 Benchmark v1.1.0 - 5.2 Client Encryption

remediation.command: Create a keystore, set client_encryption_options: {enabled: true, optional: false, keystore: ..., keystore_password: ...} in cassandra.yaml and rolling-restart; update drivers/cqlsh to use TLS.

title: Ensure a separate user and group exist for Cassandra
description: Create separate userid and group for Cassandra. The benchmark rates this recommendation Manual; the automated check covers its objective pass criterion. Passes when the cassandra group and user exist and the user is a member (primary or supplementary) of the group.
reference: CIS Apache Cassandra 5.0 Benchmark v1.1.0 - 1.1 Ensure a separate user and group exist for Cassandra

audit.command: g=$(getent group cassandra) || exit 1; u=$(getent passwd cassandra) || exit 1; gid=$(printf '%s' "$g" | cut -d: -f3); ugid=$(printf '%s' "$u" | cut -d: -f4); members=$(printf '%s' "$g" | cut -d: -f4); if [ "$gid" = "$ugid" ] || printf '%s' ",$members," | grep -q ',cassandra,'; then echo compliant; else echo 'user not in group'; fi

remediation.command: groupadd cassandra; useradd -m -d /home/cassandra -s /bin/bash -g cassandra -u <UID> cassandra (use an unused UID).

title: Ensure the latest version of Java is installed
description: A prerequisite to installing Cassandra is the installation of Java. The version of Java installed should be the most recent that is compatible with the organization's operational needs. Assessed manually here: the benchmark check is environment-specific and cannot be evaluated reliably by a single command.
reference: CIS Apache Cassandra 5.0 Benchmark v1.1.0 - 1.2 Ensure the latest version of Java is installed

audit.command: Run java -version on every node. The JDK/JRE must be a supported, fully patched release of a Java version supported by your Cassandra release (Cassandra 5.0 supports Java 11 and 17). An old or unsupported Java version is a finding.

remediation.command: 1. Uninstall the old/unsupported version of Java, if present. 2. Download the latest compatible release of the Java JDK, or OpenJDK. 3. Follow the provided installation instructions to complete the install.

title: Ensure clocks are synchronized on all nodes
description: Enabling Network Time Protocol (NTP), or some equivalent way, to keep clocks on all nodes in sync is critical. The benchmark rates this recommendation Manual; the automated check covers its objective pass criterion. Uses timedatectl (systemd); passes when the kernel clock is reported as NTP-synchronised by chronyd, ntpd or systemd-timesyncd. Compare offsets across nodes as well.
reference: CIS Apache Cassandra 5.0 Benchmark v1.1.0 - 1.6 Ensure clocks are synchronized on all nodes

remediation.command: Install and enable chrony (or ntpd) on every node, pointing all nodes at the same time sources: systemctl enable --now chronyd.

title: Ensure there are no unnecessary roles or excessive privileges
description: Verify each role is require and has only the privileges needed to do its job.
reference: CIS Apache Cassandra 5.0 Benchmark v1.1.0 - 3.3 Ensure there are no unnecessary roles or excessive privileges

audit.command: As a superuser, retrieve all roles: list roles; Retrieve all permissions for all roles select * from system_auth.role_permissions; If there are any unnecessary roles or roles with excessive privileges this is a finding.

remediation.command: Remove any unnecessary roles and/or permissions in accordance with organizational needs.

title: Ensure that Cassandra only listens for network connections on authorized interfaces
description: When listen_address is blank and listen_interface is commented out, this will be set automatically by InetAddress.getLocalHost(). Presuming the node is configured correctly, e.g. hostname, name resolution, etc., this will configure the node to use the address associated with the hostname. The listen_address must not be set to 0.0.0.0.
reference: CIS Apache Cassandra 5.0 Benchmark v1.1.0 - 3.5 Ensure that Cassandra only listens for network connections on authorized interfaces

audit.command: Run grep -nE "^(listen_address|listen_interface|rpc_address|rpc_interface):" /etc/cassandra/cassandra.yaml. Only one of listen_address/listen_interface may be set, it must name an authorised address or interface, and listen_address must not be 0.0.0.0. Any other value is a finding.

remediation.command: Set the listen_address or listen_interface, not both, in the cassandra.yaml to an authorized address or interface.

title: Ensure that Data Center Authorizations is activated
description: Authorization at Data Center level is pluggable in Cassandra and is configured using the network_authorizer setting in cassandra.yaml. Cassandra ships with AllowAllNetworkAuthorizer which allows any role to access any datacenter effectively disabling datacenter authorization; which is the current behavior. The benchmark rates this recommendation Manual; the automated check covers its objective pass criterion. Checks /etc/cassandra/cassandra.yaml (package install; SKIP when it does not exist).
reference: CIS Apache Cassandra 5.0 Benchmark v1.1.0 - 3.6 Ensure that Data Center Authorizations is activated

remediation.command: On each node set 'network_authorizer: CassandraNetworkAuthorizer' in cassandra.yaml and rolling-restart; then restrict roles with ALTER ROLE <r> WITH ACCESS TO DATACENTERS {...}.

title: Review User-Defined Roles
description: The MEMBER_OF column found in the system_auth.roles table shows roles granted to roles.
reference: CIS Apache Cassandra 5.0 Benchmark v1.1.0 - 3.7 Review User-Defined Roles

audit.command: Execute the following SQL statement to audit this setting: select role, can_login, member_of from system_auth.roles; Looking for can_login which tells you that role can log into cassandra and member_of is when roles are granted to roles.

remediation.command: Looking at those users from the query that have member_of that is NOT null, decide if that user truly needs that role, if not, for each user, issue the following SQL statement (replace <is_member> with the value of member_of returned by the query in the audit procedure) revoke <is_member> from role;

title: Ensure that logging is enabled
description: Apache Cassandra uses Logback for logging functionality. While this can be set using nodetool setlogginglevel changes made using this method will be reverted to the level specified in the logback.xml file the next time the process restarts. The configurable logging levels are: - OFF - TRACE - DEBUG - INFO (Default) - WARN - ERROR Runs nodetool getlogginglevels (JMX on localhost:7199); passes when the ROOT logger is not OFF.
reference: CIS Apache Cassandra 5.0 Benchmark v1.1.0 - 4.1 Ensure that logging is enabled

audit.command: out=$(nodetool getlogginglevels 2>/dev/null) || exit 1; printf '%s\n' "$out" | awk '$1 == "ROOT" {r = $2} END {if (r == "") print "no ROOT logger"; else if (toupper(r) == "OFF") print "OFF"; else print "compliant"}'

remediation.command: Set <root level="INFO"> in logback.xml (or logback-test.xml if present) and restart Cassandra, or run nodetool setlogginglevel ROOT INFO.

title: Ensure cassandra.yaml is not writable by group or readable by others
description: cassandra.yaml can contain keystore and truststore passwords; restrict it to mode 640 or stricter. Checks /etc/cassandra/cassandra.yaml (SKIP when it does not exist; tarball installs keep it under $CASSANDRA_HOME/conf).
reference: CIS Apache Cassandra Benchmark - File Permissions / Configuration Files (verify section number for your release)

audit.command: p=$(stat -c %a /etc/cassandra/cassandra.yaml 2>/dev/null) || exit 1; if [ $((0$p & 037)) -eq 0 ]; then echo compliant; else echo "mode $p"; fi

remediation.command: chmod 640 /etc/cassandra/cassandra.yaml

title: Ensure the latest version of Python is installed
description: A prerequisite to installing Cassandra is the installation of Python. The version of Python installed should be the most recent that is compatible with the organizations' operational needs. Assessed manually here: the benchmark check is environment-specific and cannot be evaluated reliably by a single command.
reference: CIS Apache Cassandra 5.0 Benchmark v1.1.0 - 1.3 Ensure the latest version of Python is installed

audit.command: Run python3 --version (or python -V) on hosts that use cqlsh. An old or unsupported Python release is a finding; cqlsh requires a currently supported Python 3 release.

remediation.command: 1. Uninstall the old/unsupported version of Python, if present. 2. Download the latest compatible release of the Python: https://www.python.org/downloads/ 3. Follow the provided installation instructions to complete the install.
